small_guidance:
- The GEMM is the bottleneck (M=1024, N=K=8192). Add larger autotune configs (BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32/64; BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=32) and try num_stages=4 with num_warps=8 to better overlap K-loop loads on this large K.
- Avoid the extra Wt = W.t().contiguous() copy each forward (8192×8192 fp32 = 256MB transpose). Either cache the transposed weight in __init__ as a buffer, or load B with swapped strides directly so no materialization is required.
- The partial buffers force BLOCK_N=256 for the GEMM. Decouple by making BLOCK_N a constexpr in the autotune set and sizing partials to ceil(N/BLOCK_N_min); or fuse finalize into the GEMM via atomic max/sum into per-row scratch with a second small kernel doing only the log+activation.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a single-pass online-softmax-style GEMM-LSE: persistent kernel where each program owns one (or a few) rows entirely and streams across all N tiles, maintaining (running_max, running_sumexp) in registers. With M=1024 this fits the SM count well and avoids the two-kernel split + partial materialization entirely; finalize (log + 2×LeakyReLU + 2×GELU) is then trivially fused at the end.
- Alternatively, keep the split-K-over-N structure but fuse the finalize epilogue into the GEMM by using a single column of per-row atomics (one atomic max + one atomic add of exp(local-globalmax) requires two passes). A cleaner variant: launch the GEMM tiled only over N (BLOCK_M = full row chunk like 64–128, one program per row group), so each program reduces its row in-register and writes one (max, sumexp) pair per (row, n_tile); then a tiny second kernel combines.
- Cache W (or its transpose) once in __init__ as a contiguous buffer to remove the per-call 256MB transpose copy, and pass W with strides chosen so the inner load is contiguous along K — this alone is likely a noticeable fraction of current runtime.
